title: probabilistic-reservoir-admission-and-staggered-decode-schedule-for-tail-mitigation
creator: Aisha Morales
description: Problem: Despite multiple optimizations, we still observe 95th/99th tail spikes for mixed short/long requests under sustained load. Current admission uses fixed time windows and conservative prefills which either waste kernel budgets or create long decode waits. Goal: design and implement a probabilistic reservoir-based admission controller that blends per-request urgency signals, per-tenant QoS, and kernel-hint metadata; couple it with a staggered decode schedule (micro-staggering) to smooth downstream kernel load and reduce contention on attention kernels and KV-cache eviction. The approach should be rollout-safe and allow live validation against SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce P95 latency by >= 15% and P99 by >= 25% for mixed short/long workloads on internal perf cluster compared to baseline (runtime-1.23)
No increase in median latency by more than 5% for steady-state traffic
End-to-end throughput across capacity budget remains within 5% of baseline under identical load
Feature toggles for: reservoir mode on/off, per-tenant QoS weights, kernel-hint propagation, and stagger interval configuration
Observability: new dashboards showing admission reservoir occupancy, per-kernel queue length, decode-stagger lead/lag, and a regression alert tied to our eval prompt set
design_notes: Reservoir admission: maintain a token reservoir sized by current free kernel budget (derived from kernel_time windows) and refill periodically with a decay term to avoid oscillation

Admission decision uses: (1) request urgency (deadline header), (2) token cost estimate (sequence length * cost-per-token by kernel shape), (3) tenant QoS weight, (4) randomization with tunable acceptance curve to avoid synchronized bursts

Kernel hint: attach an ordinal hint (fast-path, mixed, heavy-attn) computed at prefill to guide kernel selection during decode; runtime picks compatible kernels and preemptively reserves KV cache ranges for heavy-attn paths

Staggered decode schedule: when multiple decode-ready requests target same kernel class, schedule micro-shifts (1-10ms) based on reservoir score to desynchronize peak kernel invocation and reduce contention spikes

Fallback: when reservoir depleted, allow two degrade modes: (A) deferral window (short wait + retry into reservoir), (B) graceful fallback to smaller-quantized variant or lower-attention-path with quality-monitoring hooks
Safety: all behavior gated behind runtime feature flag and a per-cluster kill switch; default config off for Dedicated customers unless explicitly enabled
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement lightweight reservoir controller and token accounting in admission service; expose internal metrics (reservoir_level, drain_rate)
Week 2: add kernel-cost estimator using historical token latency samples; implement kernel-hint metadata in prefill phase
Week 3: implement micro-stagger scheduler in decode orchestrator and integrate with admission signals
Week 4: instrument observability (dashboard, per-tenant traces) and end-to-end integration tests on perf cluster
Week 5: run staged canary + canary rollback automation and evaluate against eval prompt set; iterate on acceptance curve and stagger window
Week 6: documentation, runbook, and broad rollout to non-production clusters followed by controlled Dedicated pilot
testing_and_validation: Synthetic mixed workload harness (50% short 8-32 tokens, 50% long 512-2048 tokens) using internal loadgen
A/B experiment: compare reservoir-on vs reservoir-off with identical load and seed using perf cluster
Chaos: add transient kernel slowdowns (GPU jitter emulator) to validate graceful fallback and observe customer impact
Quality regression: run eval prompt set to check output KL/ROUGE drift when using fallback low-attention execution
E2E latency histograms and per-kernel queue length percentiles (1/5/25/50/75/95/99) asserted in CI against thresholds
observability_requirements: New time series: admission.reservoir.level, admission.accept.rate, kernel.queue.length.{fast,mixed,heavy}
Trace spans: admission.decision, prefill.hint, decode.schedule.delay, kernel.invoke (linkable to request id)
Dashboards: Reservoir health, Kernel contention heatmap, Tail-latency trend with commit annotations
Alerts: P99 decode latency increase > 2x baseline OR reservoir.accept_rate < 10% for 60s
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overaggressive probabilistic rejection could starve low-priority tenants => Mitigation: per-tenant minimum allocation and progressive backoff
Risk: Kernel-hint mismatch causing suboptimal kernel selection => Mitigation: conservative default hints and A/B logging for model quality metrics
Risk: Staggering increases median latency for some flows => Mitigation: limit micro-stagger to paths that contribute most to P99 and keep absolute shift budget small
Risk: Complexity increases operator cognitive load => Mitigation: clear runbook, observability, and one-click rollback flag
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): unit tests and feature-flag integration
Stage 1 (perf cluster): run daily 4h stress suite and collect baseline comparisons
Stage 2 (canary): 5% of traffic on a single region with synthetic probes and automatic rollback on SLO regression
Stage 3 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h increments if thresholds pass
Stage 4 (dedicated pilot): opt-in Dedicated tenants with manual approval and support presence
